name: Gera
title: Benjamin's descendant
summary: Gera is a person mentioned several times in the Bible, primarily as a descendant of Benjamin, Jacob's youngest son. The name Gera appears in genealogies in Genesis, Judges, and Chronicles. Gera is best known as the father or ancestor of the judge Ehud and of Shimei, who cursed King David.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in Benjamin's Genealogy
keyEvents.description: Gera is listed as one of Benjamin's sons in the genealogy in Genesis. He was part of the family that went down to Egypt with Jacob.

keyEvents.title: Ancestor of the judge Ehud
keyEvents.description: Gera is mentioned as the father (or ancestor) of Ehud, the left-handed judge from Benjamin who delivered Israel from Moabite oppression.

keyEvents.title: Ehud's Assassination of King Eglon
keyEvents.description: Ehud, son of Gera, carried out a daring assassination against the Moabite king Eglon and thus freed Israel from 18 years of oppression.

keyEvents.title: Ancestor of Shimei
keyEvents.description: Gera is mentioned as the father of Shimei, the Benjamite who cursed King David when he fled from Absalom.

keyEvents.title: Shimei's Reconciliation with David
keyEvents.description: Shimei, son of Gera, met David when he returned after Absalom's rebellion and asked for forgiveness for his curses.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in the Genealogy of Chronicles
keyEvents.description: Gera appears in Benjamin's extended genealogy in 1 Chronicles, confirming his place in the tribe of Benjamin.
